title: Meeting Rooms Needed
statement:
An office booking system has a list of meetings for one day. Each meeting is [start, end] in minutes, with start < end. A meeting holds one room from start up to, but not including, end. So a meeting that ends at minute t frees its room for a meeting that starts at minute t.

Write def solution(meetings) that returns the smallest number of rooms that can host every meeting. Return 0 for an empty list.

examples.why: The LeetCode 253 example 1. [0, 30] overlaps both others, but [5, 10] ends before [15, 20] starts.
The LeetCode 253 example 2. The meetings never overlap, so one room is enough.
Each meeting ends exactly when the next starts, so one room is reused all day.

constraints: the list is in no particular order; equal meetings may repeat

think.q: What number are you really looking for?
think.a: The largest number of meetings running at the same moment. You need at least that many rooms, because those meetings all need different rooms at that moment. That many is also enough: hand out rooms in start order and reuse any room that has become free. Meetings are half-open, [start, end), so a meeting ending at 10 and one starting at 10 never overlap.

Sort by start. At 0, the first meeting takes room A. At 5, A is busy until 30: open room B. At 15, B freed at 10: reuse it. Two rooms at most: the answer is 2. The question at each start is only: has any room freed by now? The room that frees earliest is the one to check.

think.q: What is the first idea that works?
think.a: The overlap peak always happens at some meeting's start. So for each meeting's start s, count the meetings with start ≤ s < end, and return the largest count. That is O(n^2): 900 million checks for 30,000 meetings.

Intervals: sort by start, plus a min-heap of end times. The heap holds the end time of every room in use; its smallest entry is the room that frees first. For each meeting in start order, if that smallest end is ≤ the start, reuse the room (pop it). Then push this meeting's end. The heap's largest size is the answer. Sorting the starts and the ends separately and sweeping two pointers works too, with the same O(n log n).

1. Sort the meetings by start.
  2. ends = [] (a min-heap), rooms = 0.
  3. For each [s, e]: if ends is not empty and ends[0] ≤ s, heappop(ends). Then heappush(ends, e) and set rooms = max(rooms, len(ends)).
  4. Return rooms.

No meetings (0). One meeting (1). Back-to-back meetings that touch, which share one room: getting < versus ≤ wrong gives a wrong answer. Identical meetings, which each need a room. Meetings nested inside a long one. Unsorted input.

hints: The answer is the largest number of meetings that run at the same moment. Where on the timeline can that maximum happen?
Process meetings in start order. When one starts, you only care whether the room that frees earliest is free yet.
Keep the end times of rooms in use in a heapq min-heap. If ends[0] ≤ start, pop it (the room is reused); then push the new end. Track the heap's largest size.
solution:
import heapq

def solution(meetings):
    ends = []                          # min-heap: end time of each room in use
    rooms = 0
    for s, e in sorted(meetings):      # in start order
        if ends and ends[0] <= s:      # the earliest-free room is free by now
            heapq.heappop(ends)        # reuse it (ending at s frees it for s)
        heapq.heappush(ends, e)
        rooms = max(rooms, len(ends))
    return rooms
explain:
Example 4, [[1, 10], [2, 7], [3, 19], [8, 12], [10, 20], [11, 30]] (already in start order):

  • [1, 10]: heap empty, push 10. Rooms 1.
  • [2, 7]: smallest end 10 > 2, push 7. Rooms 2.
  • [3, 19]: smallest end 7 > 3, push 19. Rooms 3.
  • [8, 12]: smallest end 7 ≤ 8: pop it, push 12. Still 3 rooms in use.
  • [10, 20]: smallest end 10 ≤ 10: pop, push 20. Still 3.
  • [11, 30]: smallest end 12 > 11: push 30. Rooms 4.

Return 4: at minute 11 the meetings [3, 19], [8, 12], [10, 20] and [11, 30] all run. You pop at most one room per meeting, and that is enough: the heap only has to make room for this meeting. Rooms that freed earlier but stay in the heap do not raise the maximum, because the heap size only grows when no room is free.
complexity: O(n log n) time for the sort and the heap, O(n) space
